_comment: Declarative chat accounts, applied by bin/omarchy-thunderbird-apply.
Each account carries an integer `id` — the Thunderbird account number. Thunderbird
keys chat accounts by account<N> and enumerates them from its account manager
(imAccounts.sys.mjs initAccounts reads MailServices.accounts), so an account only
exists once mail.accountmanager.accounts lists it and a type=im incoming server with
imAccount = account<N> points at it. apply writes exactly that (plus the account's
messenger.account.account<N>.* config) into the profile's prefs.js — NOT user.js,
which would override Thunderbird's own account management and drop accounts added
later in the UI.
Pick an id no existing account uses (apply refuses a clash with a non-im account).
apply also refuses to run while Thunderbird is open (it would overwrite prefs.js on
exit). Only credential-free accounts can be declared: a password is not a preference,
it goes to the system login store, so protocols that need one (Matrix, XMPP) still
have to be added in Thunderbird's own Chat tab. IRC needs no password
(passwordOptional).
Fields:
id         Thunderbird account number (positive integer; becomes account<id>)
name       display name shown in the Chat tab
protocol   e.g. prpl-irc
username   optional; for IRC the nick, or nick@server
autoJoin   optional; comma-separated channels
autoLogin  optional boolean (default false)
Example (declared but empty, so nothing is written until you opt in):
{"id": 1, "name": "Libera", "protocol": "prpl-irc",
"username": "yournick@irc.libera.chat", "autoLogin": false}
